title: Composing iterators
hints: Each adapter returns a new iter.Seq that ranges over its input and decides what to pass on to its own yield. Values are pulled one at a time, so an infinite input such as Naturals() is fine.
Take must stop pulling from its input after n values. Returning from the inner for … range loop stops the upstream iterator. Both adapters must also stop when their own yield returns false.
Filter: for v := range seq { if keep(v) && !yield(v) { return } }. Take: if n <= 0 { return }; count := 0; for v := range seq { if !yield(v) { return }; count++; if count == n { return } }.
